key_insight: Small-radius, high-electronegativity A-site dopants such as Ca can simultaneously boost proton transport and chemical stability in BaCeO3 electrolytes by weakening A–O bonding and contracting the lattice.
engineering_relevance: A-site doping offers a practical design route for proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cell electrolytes that need both higher conductivity and better resistance to CO2/SO2 degradation.
method: Mechanistic analysis of A-site electronegativity and ionic-radius effects
Assessment of proton uptake, vacancy formation, adsorption, and segregation behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical evaluation showing improved oxygen-vacancy formation, proton uptake, reduced acidic-gas adsorption, and potential mitigation of grain-boundary resistance with Ca doping.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on composition and operating conditions, and Ca segregation or lattice changes could introduce tradeoffs in long-term microstructural stability.
paper_title: Role of small-radius and high-electronegativity A-Site dopants in enhancing proton transport and stability of perovskite electrolytes
